previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for evaluation of recurrent chest pain occurring at rest and after dialysis. Initial workup revealed nonspecific EKG changes and a stable, baseline-elevated troponin. A dipyridamole nuclear stress test showed a new reversible perfusion defect in the inferior wall, suggesting restenosis of a prior coronary stent. The patient underwent cardiac catheterization, which confirmed in-stent restenosis in the right coronary artery, and successfully received a new drug-eluting stent. He remained stable post-procedure, completed a scheduled hemodialysis session, and was discharged home in good condition. Medication changes included switching from atenolol to Toprol XL, adding lisinopril, and adjusting simvastatin and cinacalcet doses. Follow-up was arranged with a new cardiologist.

Brief Hospital Course:

of admission. His cardiac enzymes were stable and EKG was 
unchanged. Given that his presentation was different than his 
normal anginal symptoms, he had recent cath with stenting, and 
he did not have evidence of ACS, it was decided to discharge him 
with close follow-up.
